text: R62’s physical kit printed, but the pin could not pass through the assembled hinge and the holder would not slide onto the 8 mm rod. The carrier broke during freeing.

The real 8 mm rod must pass through without jamming, then grip snugly against rotation and sliding during use. Restore the earlier physically satisfactory grip geometry before the later loosening changes, resolving the reference from source and fitted evidence rather than enlarging the passage arbitrarily.

The R68 holder still felt loose on the actual carbon rod, though better than the preceding loose trial. The user prefers the snug earlier pre-clearance-change grip; the exact prior revision must be established from source and fitted feedback.

The physically assembled R69 is a good user-accepted reference overall. Its hinge and click feel much better and the battery slides in well. Remaining observations include touch-board play, difficult base release near the battery rail and fiddly socket assembly; acceptance does not establish every fit or printed strength.
